input.prompt:
You are a Frama-C ACSL annotation specialist. Your job is to generate ACSL loop annotations and function annotations for a single C file so that all original `//@ assert(...)` assertions are proven by Frama-C WP, WITHOUT modifying any original C tokens or assertions, and WITHOUT using `//@ admit`, `assume`, or `axiom`.

## Environments and exact commands

Use this exact prefix for all spectool CLI calls (do NOT use `PYTHONPATH=spectool python3 -m spectool.cli`):
```
/Users/dijkstra/ACSL-Agent\ 2/acsl模块化验证/.venv/bin/python -m engine.harness_spectool
```

Use Frama-C verify via:
```
/Users/dijkstra/ACSL-Agent\ 2/acsl模块化验证/.venv/bin/python -m engine.harness_spectool verify -f <your .acsl.c file> --timeout 15 --save-stdout <your .wp.txt file>
```
Use locate-fail via:
```
/Users/dijkstra/ACSL-Agent\ 2/acsl模块化验证/.venv/bin/python -m engine.harness_spectool locate-fail --wp <wp.txt> --src <.acsl.c>
```

Hard rule: NEVER add `//@ admit`, `assume`, or `axiom`. Only add ACSL loop invariants, loop assigns, loop variants, and function contracts. Do not weaken or remove original assertions.

## Input files

Verification target stub (read this; inject into a copy):
`[TASK]/workspace/output/layer0/main/main.c`

Inline reference (read-only, same code, for understanding):
`[TASK]/workspace/output/layer0/main/main.inline.c`

## What the program does

`main()` declares three VLA arrays `a[N]`, `b[N]`, `c[N]` with `N=100000`. `unknown()` has a contract: `assigns \nothing; ensures -100000 < \result < 100000;`.

- Loop 1 (i from 0 to N): `x = unknown(); assert(x > -100000 && x < 100000); a[i]=x; b[i]=-x;`
- Loop 2 (i from 0 to N): `c[i]=a[i]+b[i];`
- Loop 3 (i from 1 to N): `assert(c[i] == 0);`

You must prove all asserts. Key knowledge: in loop 1, `b[j]==-a[j]` for every j, so in loop 2 `c[j]=a[j]+b[j]=0`. The asserts in loop 3 need the full-range knowledge `\forall j; 0<=j<N ==> c[j]==0`.

## Suggested annotation approach (adapt as needed)

Loop 1:
```
/*@
  loop invariant 0 <= i <= N;
  loop invariant \forall integer j; 0 <= j < i ==> b[j] == -a[j];
  loop assigns i, x, a[0 .. N-1], b[0 .. N-1];
  loop variant N - i;
*/
```
(Note `x` is reassigned inside the loop, so include it in loop assigns. The assert inside comes from `unknown()`'s `ensures`.)

Loop 2:
```
/*@
  loop invariant 0 <= i <= N;
  loop invariant \forall integer j; 0 <= j < N ==> b[j] == -a[j];
  loop invariant \forall integer j; 0 <= j < i ==> c[j] == 0;
  loop assigns i, c[0 .. N-1];
  loop variant N - i;
*/
```

Loop 3:
```
/*@
  loop invariant 1 <= i <= N;
  loop invariant \forall integer j; 0 <= j < N ==> c[j] == 0;
  loop assigns i;
  loop variant N - i;
*/
```

If WP reports stability/assigns issues due to the multiple VLA arrays, you may try adding a `//@ \separated(...)` as a plain ACSL annotation (NOT admit) — but first confirm whether WP needs it. Prefer loop invariants with full-range knowledge.

## Procedure

1. Copy the stub to your working file in the SAME directory:
   `[TASK]/workspace/output/layer0/main/main.acsl.c`
2. Use the `inject` spectool command to insert the loop annotation blocks at the correct lines (the `for` keyword lines in the stub), OR directly write main.acsl.c by hand including the ACSL annotations. Either way the original tokens/assertions must be unchanged and the ACSL annotations added.
3. Run `verify` on main.acsl.c saving stdout to `main.wp.txt` in the same directory.
4. If verify fails, run `locate-fail` and fix the annotations (up to 5 rounds), re-verify until `proved == total` and result is Pass.
5. Verify result JSON should have `"result": "Pass"`.

## Final report

Return a JSON object (and brief summary) to me:
```json
{
  "status": "pass" | "fail",
  "proved": <int goals proved>,
  "total": <int total goals>,
  "round": <int>,
  "tokens": <estimated int>
}
```
Only report "pass" if proved == total. Do NOT print the .acsl.c content in full; just report status. Ensure the artifacts exist at the paths above.
